title: Strategic Customer Success Manager
description:
A little about us

incident.io is the AI software reliability platform trusted by engineering teams at Netflix, Etsy, and 2,000+ companies who can't afford downtime.

The stakes are real, the talent is insane, and somehow it's a genuinely lovely place to work. We all pull our weight, go the extra mile, and put in the bit of magic most companies don't have time for, all while having fun and never taking ourselves too seriously.

We've raised $100+ million from Index Ventures, Insight Partners, and Point Nine, and we're growing fast. There's never been a better time to join.

The role in one line

As our first EMEA Strategic Customer Success Manager, you’ll help define what strategic success looks like at incident.io , and become the trusted partner who makes us core to how the biggest enterprises run reliability.

What that looks like day to day

You’ll work with a small number of our largest, most complex and highest-value customers. These are established, often global and regulated enterprises, where buying decisions take time, many business units are involved, and incident management is part of a wider move away from legacy tools and processes. You’ll be their strategic partner across the full lifecycle, from early involvement in the deal with Sales through to adoption and expansion, and from the on-call engineer to the CIO and CTO.

You’ll help land strategic logos with focused first contracts, then build the business case and success plan that turns them into larger deals. From there you’ll expand across the enterprise, mapping the organisation, finding champions and repeating proven wins across business units and regions. You’ll run Executive Business Reviews and connect our leadership with theirs, tying what we do to what matters to their business: operational resilience, regulatory risk, the cost of downtime, tool consolidation, MTTR reduction and incident process maturity.

You’ll lead onboarding and migrations in organisations that move carefully, moving them off legacy tools and ITSM-led processes and making the change stick, including deeper adoption across Response, On-call, Status Pages and our AI capabilities. You’ll spot and reduce business, operational and reputational risk before it becomes visible, and bring Sales, Solutions Engineering, Product, Marketing and Support together around shared goals for each account, including expansion and renewals.

You’ll also work directly with Product and Engineering on the roadmap and design partnerships. As the first EMEA Strategic CSM and third on the team overall, you’ll help define our strategic CS playbook, support high-stakes deals and help develop your peers as the segment grows.

Who you are

- You have significant experience in Customer Success, Account Management or Technical Account Management, managing strategic or Fortune 500-scale accounts in enterprise SaaS. Traditional enterprises like financial services, insurance, pharma, retail or private equity are ideal. Developer tooling, observability or incident management is a plus.

- You’ve driven adoption, retention and expansion in large, complex accounts with many stakeholders, and you have results you can point to.

- You know how to land small and grow large, turning a pilot or single business unit into a multi-BU footprint over a long sales cycle.

- Building a business case doesn’t faze you, nor does navigating procurement, security, legal and change management in slow-moving organisations.

- You’re confident with senior technical executives, running EBRs and strategic planning sessions, and just as comfortable going deep with SREs and platform engineers.

- You’re technically fluent in modern engineering organisations, on-call, incident response, SRE practices and the observability and DevOps ecosystem, and you can translate it for business stakeholders.

- You have strong commercial judgement, partner well with Sales on renewals and expansion, and get ahead of customer challenges rather than reacting to them.

- You’re autonomous and comfortable with ambiguity. You’re excited to define the role, not just step into it.

Supporting you

We work hard and we think life outside work matters just as much. Our benefits pack is built to support both.

- Private medical insurance. Seriously good cover - we want you and the people you love to be looked after.

- Competitive annual leave. Showing up at your best requires switching off, and we make sure you have time to do that.

- First Friday of every month off. Yes, seriously.

- Enhanced pension. We put real money in, because future-you deserves better than an afterthought.

- Meaningful equity. We’re rapidly scaling, and everyone who helps shape the outcome should share in it.

- Unlimited AI spend. For everyone, not just engineers. We’re all-in on AI across the company, and we expect you to be too.

- Generous parental leave. The early days with a new baby matter more than anything we’re doing here, and we want you to be present for them.

- Two budgets that have your back. £1000 to invest in your setup, £500 a year to invest in yourself.

title: Director of Quality
description:
About LILT 

AI is changing how the world communicates — and LILT is leading that transformation. 

We're on a mission to make the world's information accessible to everyone , regardless of the language they speak. We use cutting-edge AI, machine translation, and human-in-the-loop expertise to translate content faster, more accurately, and more cost-effectively without compromising on brand, voice, or quality.

At LILT, we empower our teammates with leading tools, global collaboration, and growth opportunities to do their best work. Our company virtues— Work together, win together; Find a way or make one; Dance in the customer's shoes; Quicker than they expect; Quality is Job 1 —guide everything we do. We are trusted by Intel Corporation , Canva , the United States Department of Defense , the United States Air Force , ASICS , and hundreds of global Enterprises. Backed by Sequoia, Intel Capital, and Redpoint, we’re building a category-defining company in a $50B+ global translation market being redefined by AI.

Location: Remote or hybrid, EMEA or US Eastern time zone

Team: Production, Quality

Reports to: VP Production

Direct reports: Quality Manager (AMER, customer staffing) and 2 Quality Coordinators

About the role

As Director of Quality, you will own LILT's quality system end to end: standards, audit, compliance, procedures, continuous improvement, and the roadmap and operation of our Quality Agents . You'll help move Quality from a primarily reactive, execution-led function to a proactive, data-driven partner for customers and internal teams, with quality designed into our AI-native workflows.

You'll be the person who can run a customer audit while simultaneously shipping an improved agent evaluation. As the single Quality partner for Customer Success, Production, Research and Product, you'll turn customer requirements into measurable acceptance criteria, effective controls and better models and workflows. You'll advise customers on the right quality, cost and speed mix, including where automated, agent-verified and human-verified workflows are appropriate, with stronger assurance for high-risk and regulated content.

We're looking for a hands-on Quality SME and operator with real depth in both worlds: experience designing and building AI agents and improving LLM output, and a solid grounding in traditional quality management. You'll bring senior expertise in data, AI, customer advisory and process, and make sure quality work prevents recurrence rather than stopping at rework or ticket closure.

What you'll do

Quality Agent leadership 

- Evaluate, design and build reliable Quality Agents with well-defined tools and clear, structured instructions.

- Use orchestration patterns to evolve from a single agent to multi-agent systems.

- Define evaluation criteria, test sets and success metrics for agent performance, and run agents in production with clear monitoring and escalation paths.

- Drive adoption across teams and show measurable reductions in manual quality effort.

Research and Product partnership 

- Work closely with Research and Product on ADQ, LLM model improvements, AI Review, AI QA, and new and emerging AI workflows.

- Turn quality findings into product requirements, evaluation criteria and continuous feedback loops that improve model and workflow output.

- Act as the voice of quality in roadmap discussions, and help decide where human review, AI review or both are needed.

Audit, compliance and procedure 

- Own LILT's approach to internal and external audits, including ISO certification (e.g. ISO 17100, ISO 18587, ISO 9001) and customer audits.

- Plan and run periodic internal audits, manage evidence collection, and track corrective and preventive actions to closure.

- Standardise and maintain SOPs, workflows and quality documentation, and keep them current as AI workflows change how we work.

- Make sure quality processes meet customer, contractual and regulatory requirements.

Customer advisory 

- Partner with Customer Success and Delivery to define proactive quality programmes, success metrics and governance for strategic accounts, including AI-forward enterprise and life science / regulatory programmes.

- Translate customer quality requirements into clear pre-delivery acceptance criteria, validation methods and risk-appropriate controls.

- Advise customers on the right quality, cost and speed mix and where automated, agent-verified, human-verified or combined workflows are appropriate.

- Represent LILT's quality function as a credible subject-matter authority in customer business reviews, audits and escalations, using quality data and metrics to demonstrate fitness for purpose.

Continuous improvement

The Opportunity 

SINGU provides property and facilities management technology for organisations operating complex, multi-site estates . Retail is a strategically important market for the business, spanning shopping centres, retail parks, high-street portfolios, supermarkets, hospitality and other distributed consumer environments.

We are seeking an experienced retail property, facilities or operations leader to become SINGU's senior market authority for retail and help build a differentiated, commercially successful position in the sector.

This is not a conventional sales, pre-sales, product marketing or communications role . It is a senior, market-facing position for someone who understands retail property and operations at practitioner level and can translate that experience, credibility and network into measurable commercial impact .

Success will be measured not simply through market visibility or activity, but through SINGU's ability to create qualified pipeline , win strategic customers , expand existing relationships and establish a repeatable position within priority retail segments .

Within the first 12 months , you will have established a clear and credible retail go-to-market strategy , identifying the segments and use cases where SINGU can win disproportionately and building meaningful executive relationships across priority retail accounts .

You will have originated and influenced significant qualified pipeline , contributed demonstrably to both new-logo and expansion revenue , and developed repeatable retail propositions supported by clear customer evidence .

You will also have strengthened SINGU's network of retail customers and advocates , while materially increasing our credibility, relevance and market position within the retail property and facilities sector.

What You Will Own 

Retail Market Strategy: 

- Define where SINGU has the strongest right to win across retail.

- Shape our retail go-to-market strategy , priority segments, use cases and target accounts .

- Maintain a strong point of view on the operational, regulatory and technology issues shaping retail estates.

- Translate market insight into clear commercial and product priorities .

Executive Access and Market Development: 

- Build trusted relationships with senior leaders across retail property, facilities, operations, asset management and transformation.

- Use your network and industry credibility to create access to strategic prospects and originate new opportunities .

- Represent SINGU in executive forums , customer meetings, roundtables and selected industry events .

- Build relationships across the wider retail ecosystem , including advisers, FM providers, managing agents and partners.

Strategic Accounts and Commercial Impact: 

- Work with Sales and Customer Success on a focused portfolio of priority retail accounts .

- Help uncover strategic priorities, strengthen business cases and improve executive engagement .

- Support selected opportunities where your involvement can materially increase SINGU's probability of winning .

- Identify expansion opportunities across customers, countries, sites, modules and use cases.

- Contribute directly to qualified pipeline and revenue growth , without replacing the accountable salesperson .

Customer and Market Insight: 

- Build a strong community of retail customers, advocates and industry influencers .

- Bring structured market insight into Product, Product Marketing and Commercial Strategy.

- Identify repeatable customer needs , emerging opportunities and gaps in SINGU's proposition.

- Help ensure SINGU invests in problems that customers are willing to pay to solve .

Commercial Accountability: 

This is not a conventional quota-carrying role , but it has clear commercial accountability . Performance will be measured against:

- qualified pipeline originated and materially influenced;

- revenue contribution from strategic retail opportunities;

- progression and penetration of priority accounts;

- executive relationships created within target organisations;

- development of repeatable retail propositions and use cases ;

- customer advocacy and market influence .

Specific commercial targets will be agreed annually .

What We're Looking For: 

- Significant senior experience in retail property, facilities management, estates, operations or asset management.

- First-hand understanding of complex, multi-site retail estates .

- Strong credibility and an established network with senior retail stakeholders .

- Evidence of turning industry relationships and insight into commercial opportunities or strategic outcomes.

- Strong commercial judgement and the ability to connect operational challenges to financial value, risk and business outcomes .

- Executive presence , strong communication skills and the confidence to challenge senior stakeholders constructively .

- The ability to identify what is genuinely scalable and commercially valuable , rather than simply interesting.

- Business-fluent English ; Polish and/or German language is an advantage

Package and Progression:

- Performance-related bonus linked to strategic-account engagement, market influence and measurable commercial contribution.

- Direct sponsorship from the CRO and access to SINGU's executive leadership .

- Support from Sales, Marketing, Product Marketing, Product and Pre-Sales .

- The opportunity to shape SINGU's retail market position across Europe .

- Progression into broader market leadership , strategic growth or industry-led go-to-market responsibility.

title: Engineering Delivery & Operations Manager
description:
Joining Weezevent means working on tangible solutions used at international festivals (Hellfest, Boomtown, Tomorrowland, Lollapalooza, Boom), major sporting events (Formula 1, the Olympic Games, Euro fan zones), and high-volume live experiences.

Weezevent builds the technology behind live events: ticketing , cashless payment , CRM , staff solutions and access control . We are about 100 people in the tech team (engineering and product organisation), part of a group that has grown both organically and through acquisitions, so our teams span several countries and cultures.

We are at an inflection point. We are opening a focused 12–18 month window to invest heavily in the foundations of our main product, WeezTicket: paying down technical debt, tightening our architecture, and setting ourselves up for the next phase of growth. To run that program, we’re hiring an Engineering Delivery & Operations Manager (M/F, based in Clichy) to own its delivery.

Vos missions

This is a two-part role, and the first part is where you’ll spend most of your first year.

Part one : deliver the program . A board of our most experienced engineers is defining the architectural direction and producing a large backlog of clean-up and improvement work. That work will be delivered by several external squads brought in for the program. You own the delivery layer between them: getting squads stood up and productive on time, tracking each one’s pace and quality, and keeping the whole program on schedule.

- Stand up and onboard external squads, around 20 developers across 5 to 6 squads, on time : access, environments, documentation, and a well-scoped first backlog ready before they start

- Track the delivery pace of each squad against its commitments, and keep a clear program-level view of what’s on track, slipping, or blocked

- Hold squads to the quality bar set by the architectural board : tests, reviews, and no new debt introduced while removing old debt

- Manage cross-squad dependencies so work lands in the right order

- Track program spend against budget and manage the relationships with the partners supplying the squads

- Report program status to the CTO and the board on a regular cadence

Part two : become the operational backbone of engineering. As the program matures, you’ll take on the people-operations side of the organisation: helping our managers run great 1:1s and reviews, coordinating the performance cycle, keeping an eye on team capacity and wellbeing, and bringing rigour to tooling and budget. This is what makes the role a long-term home rather than a temporary program job.

You’ll work closely with the CTO, the architectural board, our 4 Team Leads, and the external partners supplying the squads. You won’t set the technical strategy or write the code, you’ll make sure the right work gets delivered, on time, at the right quality.

- Help 4 Team Leads and 6 Squad Leads run consistent 1:1s and grow as managers

- Coordinate the performance review cycle and make sure follow-up actions actually happen

- Keep visibility on team capacity, absences, and early signals of overload or burnout

- Bring structure to tech budget tracking and to the governance of our tools and licences

- Support hiring and internal mobility alongside our recruitment team

Vos compétences

Must-haves 

- Experience running a multi-squad delivery program end to end: ideally involving external agencies, consultancies, or contract teams

- A track record of onboarding external teams onto an existing codebase and getting them productive quickly

- Comfort owning a backlog, a schedule, and a budget across several parallel workstreams at once

- The ability to track pace and quality per team and raise problems early, with data

- Genuine tech literacy: you understand what developers do, can navigate a Jira board, and know what technical debt actually means

- Fluent French and English

What makes you a strong long-term fit 

- Some experience coaching or supporting managers, or running a performance cycle in a tech company

- A background that touched engineering, delivery, project management, or product before moving toward operations

- Analytical rigour: you’re comfortable with numbers, dashboards, and cost reports

- Direct, honest communication and real discretion with sensitive information

Nice to have 

- A third language (German or Dutch is a real plus given our footprint)

- Experience working across France, the UK, the Netherlands, or Germany, and an understanding of how management styles differ across them

This is not 

- A role that sets architecture or writes code; that’s the board and the squads

- A pure recruiter or a corporate-HR profile with no delivery or engineering exposure

- A process-for-process’s-sake job. We want impact, not bureaucracy

The recruitment process 

- HR interview - background and soft skills

- Interview with CTO - technical discussion

All our positions are open to people with disabilities. 

Why it's a good move 

You’ll run a high-visibility program with the direct backing of the CTO and the most senior engineers in the company, in an organisation that has decided to genuinely invest in its technical foundations rather than just talk about it. And when the program lands, you’ll have built yourself a permanent, central role at the heart of how our engineering organisation runs.

title: Product manager - gestion des projets (CDI)
description:
🧱 À propos de Bricks 

Chez Bricks, on construit la façon la plus simple d’investir dans l’immobilier, à partir de 10 €. 670 000+ membres, un produit régulé (PSFP) et une même exigence sur toute l’expérience : permettre d’investir simplement mais aussi de suivre son investissement dans la durée.

Bricks est une plateforme à deux faces : d’un côté les investisseurs , de l’autre les porteurs de projets immobiliers . Deux communautés à accompagner et faire grandir en parallèle. 

Ce qui se passe après le financement d’un projet compte donc autant que le moment où l’on investit : qualité de l’information, transparence, suivi des projets et gestion des situations plus complexes participent directement à l’expérience des deux côtés de la plateforme.

Quelques jalons d’une aventure assez unique : passage chez Capital (M6) en 2022, Tony Parker investisseur et ambassadeur, record européen de vitesse de levée : 5 M€ en 5 secondes, 20 M€+ en 10 jours auprès de notre communauté.

Côté business : 176 M€ collectés en 2025, +90 % en un an et la rentabilité atteinte. Notre prochain enjeu : scaler à grande échelle sans perdre la vélocité qui fait aujourd’hui partie de notre manière de travailler.

Chez Bricks, on attend de chacun qu’il comprenne vraiment les problèmes avant de chercher à les résoudre. L’objectif : prendre les bonnes décisions et construire des solutions utiles. 

Sur ce poste, ton travail aura un impact direct sur la qualité du suivi des projets et sur la confiance des investisseurs comme des porteurs de projets. 

Vos missions

🧩 Le job 

Tu rejoins la squad gestion des projets qui est en charge de tout ce qui se passe après le financement d’un projet immobilier.

Aujourd’hui, Bricks gère environ 400 projets financés simultanément . Pour chacun d’eux, il faut suivre ce qui se passe sur le terrain : récupérer les bonnes informations auprès des porteurs de projets, communiquer régulièrement avec les investisseurs et lorsque quelque chose se passe moins bien, il faut savoir gérer les impayés, les pénalités et les éventuelles procédures de contentieux.

C’est aussi ce qui fait de la gestion post-financement l’un des sujets les plus stratégiques pour Bricks . Une plateforme d’investissement ne se construit pas uniquement au moment où un utilisateur décide d’investir : elle se construit dans la durée, dans la qualité du suivi et dans la façon dont les situations plus complexes sont prises en charge.

Le challenge n’est pas simplement de “gérer 400 projets”. Il est de construire un système capable d’en gérer demain beaucoup plus sans faire grossir l’équipe au même rythme.

Une plateforme existe déjà et accompagne l’équipe au quotidien. Elle a atteint un niveau de maturité où les prochains problèmes ne se résoudront pas uniquement avec de nouvelles features : parfois la meilleure réponse sera produit, parfois process, parfois automatisation, parfois juridique.

C’est là que tu interviens.

👉 Ce que tu vas owner 

- Comprendre profondément le quotidien des utilisateurs internes en particulier celui de la personne qui opère nos projets au quotidien : observer, écouter, identifier les irritants et comprendre ce qui peut être supprimé, automatisé ou mieux structuré.

- Faire évoluer la gestion de plusieurs centaines de projets pour qu’elle reste fluide et scalable : priorisation, automatisation, workflows, process et outils.

- Travailler avec l’engineering pour transformer les problèmes identifiés en solutions produit lorsqu’une solution technique est pertinente.

- Aller chercher l’information là où elle se trouve : care, juridique, marketing, métier, engineering… Tu ne travailles pas à partir d’une spec parfaite, tu reconstruis toi-même le contexte.

- T’approprier des sujets parfois complexes ou réglementaires. Tu n’as pas besoin d’être juriste, mais un contrat de 50 pages ou une discussion sur un process de contentieux ne doit pas te faire fuir.

- Choisir le bon levier plutôt que la feature par défaut : modifier un process peut parfois avoir plus d’impact que développer un nouvel écran.

- Transformer chaque problème rencontré en apprentissage réutilisable : l’objectif n’est pas de traiter le problème du projet n°237, mais de faire en sorte qu’il soit mieux géré pour les centaines de projets suivants.

- Et progressivement, prendre de plus en plus d’ownership sur la stratégie et la roadmap de la squad . Le périmètre pourra évoluer fortement selon ce que tu démontres sur le terrain.

👥 La squad 

Tu travailleras au quotidien avec les équipes en charge du suivi opérationnel des projets ainsi qu’avec l'Engineering, le Product, le Growth et Marketing.

Selon les sujets, tu seras également amené à collaborer avec le Care, le juridique ou la direction. Un même problème peut avoir des conséquences très différentes selon les équipes et les utilisateurs concernés.

C’est un rôle où la collaboration compte énormément. Ton travail ne consiste pas simplement à recueillir les besoins de chacun et à les transformer en features. 

Tu dois aller chercher l’information directement auprès des personnes concernées, comprendre leur réalité opérationnelle, croiser les différents points de vue et remonter à la vraie problématique derrière une demande. 

Ce qu’un utilisateur te demande n’est pas toujours la solution dont il a besoin. À toi d’agréger le contexte, de challenger les demandes et de construire avec l’équipe la réponse la plus efficace qu’elle soit produit, process, technique ou juridique. 

Vos compétences

🎯 Tu fitteras si 

- Tu as au moins 3 ans d’expérience en Product Management avec déjà une vraie autonomie sur ton périmètre.

- Tu as déjà travaillé sur un produit ou un environnement où il fallait comprendre le métier avant de construire la solution . Tu vas spontanément parler aux utilisateurs plutôt que d’attendre qu’un besoin parfaitement formulé arrive jusqu’à toi. C’est un point particulièrement important pour ce rôle.

- Tu es à l’aise dans des environnements mouvants. Tu peux passer plusieurs jours à creuser un problème complexe, puis devoir jongler entre plusieurs sujets dans la même journée. Tu sais récupérer rapidement le contexte, identifier ce qui compte et avancer sans te perdre dans l’information

- Tu as un vrai mindset builder/entrepreneur : tu n’as pas besoin que tout soit déjà structuré pour commencer à avancer.

- Tu sais travailler avec des experts sans avoir besoin de devenir toi-même expert de chaque sujet. Tu peux échanger avec un juriste, un développeur, le care ou le marketing, absorber leur contexte et transformer tout ça en décisions produit cohérentes.

- Tu sais défendre un point de vue et challenger quand c’est nécessaire y compris face à des interlocuteurs très seniors, tout en étant capable de changer d’avis quand les arguments sont meilleurs.

- Une expérience dans un environnement régulé ou à fortes contraintes métier : fintech, legaltech, comptabilité, RH… est un vrai plus. Ici une décision produit peut avoir des conséquences financières, juridiques ou opérationnelles réelles.

- Tu préfères faire beaucoup avec une petite équipe plutôt que de construire du process pour construire du process

❌ Tu ne fitteras probablement pas si 

- Tu as besoin d’un framework très établi pour fonctionner.

- Tu attends des specs détaillées avant d’aller chercher toi-même le contexte.

- Ton premier réflexe face à un problème est systématiquement de créer une feature.

- Tu cherches à appliquer « la bonne méthode produit » indépendamment du contexte.

- Tu préfères passer trois semaines à cadrer parfaitement un sujet plutôt que tester rapidement une hypothèse lorsque le risque le permet.

- Ou tu imagines le rôle de PM comme quelqu’un qui organise le travail d’une squad depuis Jira : ici le Product Manager met vraiment les mains dans le problème .

Avantages

🚀 Pourquoi ce rôle est intéressant 

La squad est déjà l’une des plus matures chez Bricks mais le terrain de jeu devant elle reste énorme.

Aujourd’hui, il y a environ 400 projets. Demain, il peut y en avoir 2 000 avec de nouvelles typologies de produits, de nouveaux pays et de nouveaux enjeux réglementaires ou opérationnels. L’objectif n’est pas de construire une organisation lourde pour absorber cette croissance mais bien de trouver une meilleure façon de travailler à chaque étape .

Et à mesure que tu prends ownership du sujet, ton rôle pourra aller bien au-delà de l’exécution d’une roadmap : comprendre suffisamment bien le métier pour contribuer directement aux prochains sujets sur lesquels Bricks doit investir. 

L'offre 

👉 CDI, temps plein.

👉 De vrais sujets, un vrai impact : produit régulé, vraies conséquences quand on se plante.

👉 Beaucoup d’ownership : tu travailleras directement avec les personnes qui font le produit et tu auras une vraie influence sur ce qu’on construit.

👉Une boîte ambitieuse, rentable et en forte croissance : tu arrives à un moment où l’organisation Product est encore suffisamment petite pour que tu puisses réellement contribuer à la construire.

👉 Salaire compétitif, assurance santé moderne, MacBook Pro de ton choix, tout le matériel qu'il te faut.

👉 Hybride Montpellier : office-first (2j/sem de remote) ou remote-first (~2j/mois au bureau).

Déroulement des entretiens 

- Pré-qualification téléphonique avec notre recruteuse

- Echange métier (1h)

- Entretien team-fit (1h)

- Rencontre avec Cédric, notre fondateur (45 min)

- Offre

title: Head of Brand/Content H/F
description:
Make Sense, aujourd'hui c'est +23 000 abonnés sur LinkedIn, 8 000 sur YouTube et un positionnement différenciant sur le marché des agences marketing.

L'objectif est de faire de Make Sense et de ses dirigeants une référence visible, désirable et incontournable sur le marché, en transformant l'agence en véritable « "media company" autour d'un point de vue fort et de preuves clients massives.

Le Head of Brand est l'architecte et l'orchestrateur de la brand (corporate + personal brands des founders), pas juste un "content manager". Il s'assure que chaque contenu, chaque touchpoint, chaque cas client renforce le positionnement Make Sense.

Vos missions

Mission principale 

À 12 mois, construire et piloter un système de brand et de contenu qui :

- positionne Make Sense comme la référence des agences d'acquisition payante pour e-commerçants ambitieux,

- installe les dirigeants comme figures d'autorité sur le sujet,

- génère une demande inbound qualifiée et récurrente,

- crée de la préférence de marque et de la confiance avant même le premier call.

Cette mission s'inscrit dans un objectif à plus long terme (24-36 mois) : faire de Make Sense l'agence de performance marketing de référence en France.

Reporting & périmètre 

Reporte à Maxence CEO / Founder.

Collabore étroitement avec : Senior Strategist, Sales, équipe externe (montage, graphisme).

Make Sense est une agence pilotée par son fondateur : Maxence reste le décisionnaire final sur les grands choix de marque et de positionnement. Le rôle du Head of Brand est de nourrir sa réflexion, de la challenger avec des arguments solides, et de transformer ses convictions en système de marque et de contenu qui tourne. Autonomie totale attendu sur l'exécution et la mise en place.

Objectifs & livrables 

À 15 jours : 

- Connaître sur le bout des doigts les offres de l'agence.

- Être capable de positionner Make Sense au sein de son environnement concurrentiel et de son marché.

À 1 mois : 

- Une routine de contenus mise en place et qui commence à se roder.

- Une première capacité d'analyse des impacts (vues, engagement, retours) pour ajuster la stratégie.

À 3 mois : 

- Une proposition structurée, construite pour atteindre les objectifs à 12 mois, avec une feuille de route priorisée et des premiers arbitrages.

- Un calendrier éditorial structuré à 90 jours, mis à jour en rolling.

À 12 mois : 

- Une machine de contenu corporate + founder-led qui tourne et une cadence tenue sur l'année avec la capacité à scaler la production sans brûler les founders.

- Des process de production et de distribution documentés, et une équipe média externe qui exécute sans friction avec un Minimum Viable Squad brand/media structuré (pool de freelances ou éventuels internes) dont les rôles sont clairs.

- Une croissance claire des indicateurs brand : vues, reach qualifié, abonnés sur les bons canaux, trafic direct / branded search.

- Une croissance du volume de leads inbound qualifiés issus des contenus.

- Des feedbacks marché tangibles sur les calls de vente (« je vous suis depuis X mois », « j'ai vu telle étude de cas »).

Activités clés au quotidien 

- Traduire les objectifs business en roadmap brand & contenu.

- Réaliser et faire valider les créas et contenus (idées, scripts, tournages, montages, posts).

- Travailler main dans la main avec les founders pour extraire les idées, les frameworks, les prises de position.

- Prioriser les sujets et campagnes qui créent le plus de levier business et brand.

- Suivre les chiffres brand & inbound, ajuster les stratégies et formats.

- Garantir la cohérence : chaque output doit ressembler à « Make Sense », pas à n'importe quelle agence.

Vos compétences

Profil recherché 

Expérience 

- 5 à 8 ans d'expérience en brand / content / media, idéalement en agence (RP, social, growth, création) plutôt qu'en grand groupe pour être à l'aise dans une structure où tout va vite et où les rôles ne sont pas cloisonnés.

- Expérience significative en BtoB, ou en environnement mixte BtoB/BtoC avec une vraie culture business.

- Idéalement, une expérience de personal branding ou d'accompagnement de dirigeants sur leur prise de parole (LinkedIn, contenu, storytelling).

- A déjà construit ou contribué à un programme de contenu structuré (pas seulement géré des réseaux sociaux au fil de l'eau).

- A déjà structuré et managé une petite équipe interne ou de freelances

Mindset 

- Stratégique et tactique : voit la brand comme un levier business.

- À l'aise avec des dirigeants très visibles, capable de les challenger sans jamais lisser ou aseptiser leur discours.

- Orienté résultats.

Compétences « hard » 

- Excellente compréhension du branding B2B / agence / service premium.

- Solide culture contenu (YouTube, LinkedIn, podcasts, storytelling, formats qui convertissent en confiance).

- Capacité à bâtir et piloter un système de production de contenus.

- Bon niveau en copywriting.

- Capacité à briefer et diriger des créatifs (vidéo, design, etc.).

- À l'aise avec les chiffres : sait définir et suivre les bons KPIs.

Culture fit 

- Parle le langage business : comprend MRR, marge, LTV, CPA, etc.

- Communique clairement, sait dire non aux idées qui diluent la brand.

- Relie systématiquement ses choix créatifs et éditoriaux à des objectifs business (pas de contenu pour le contenu, pas de branding pour l'esthétique).

- Capable de travailler dans un environnement exigeant, avec des décisions qui se prennent vite et un fondateur impliqué.

- Connaît et suit Alex Hormozi : l'agence est structurée autour de la méthode VAM (Value Acceleration Method), qui nous accompagne depuis 2024 et qui structure notre feuille de route business.

- Style : direct, concret, orienté action, mais capable de profondeur sur le thinking.

Avantages

Les conditions : 

- CDI - Cadre 37,5h

- Basé en métropole lilloise (Bondues) avec télétravail

- Salaire fixe + variable déplafonné

- Tickets restaurant, mutuelle et prévoyance pris en charge à 100 %

Vous mettez en œuvre les procédures réglementaires en matière d’ hygiène, de sécurité et de salubrité publique , notamment dans le cadre du Code général des collectivités territoriales (CGCT), du Code de la santé publique (CSP), du Code de la construction et de l’habitation (CCH), du Code de l’environnement et du Règlement sanitaire départemental (RSD) .

- Apporter son expertise et contribuer à la préparation des prises de décision de son/sa responsable de service ;

- Intervenir dans la gestion des nuisances et conflits de voisinage lorsque les pouvoirs de police du Maire sont applicables.

Missions spécifiques:

Contrôler la sécurité de l’environnement de friches industrielles, produits toxiques et substances dangereuses

title: Co-founder / Treuhänder/in – let's build the Treuhand of 2030
description:
Build the Treuhand of 2030.

Co-founder wanted: certified fiduciary (Treuhänder/in).

We believe that by 2030 at the latest, AI agents will handle most routine work in a Treuhand. That leaves fiduciaries with the work that needs judgment: reviewing, advising clients and signing off.

We are founding that Treuhand for Swiss startups and SMEs. AI agents prepare the work, and a qualified fiduciary signs off everything that goes to clients and authorities.

Underneath runs a finance stack built for agents, with clean data, a full audit trail and connections to the systems clients already use. Long term, we aim to run our clients' whole finance function on this stack, from bookkeeping to reporting, planning and investor/board updates.

Where we stand

The company is not founded yet. We are testing the problem in interviews with founders, CFOs and fiduciaries, three startups are interested in a paid pilot, and we have built a first prototype. You would join from day one and build the company with me. We will add a technical co-founder at a later stage.

Who you would work with

I'm Jonas Baer, two-time entrepreneur and fractional CFO for Swiss startups. As a Venturelab trainer and Innosuisse expert, I work closely with Swiss founders, the clients we want to serve. Before that I was CFO and director at a startup where we grew revenue to almost CHF 10M and the team to over 40. I studied Business Informatics at UZH and bridge finance and IT (linkedin.com/in/jonas-baer).

What you would do

- Decide which workflows we automate first, where the AI acts alone and where a fiduciary signs

- Teach the agents Swiss practice (MWST, AHV/BVG/UVG, booking rules) and test them on real documents

- Serve the first pilot clients yourself

- Build and lead the operations team as we scale

You have the final say on what gets booked, filed and signed.

What you bring

- Treuhänder/in mit eidg. Fachausweis or dipl. Treuhandexperte/-in (or comparable)

- 4+ years of experience with SMEs and startups

- Hands-on with accounting systems such as Abacus, Bexio or Odoo (migration experience is a plus)

- Daily user of AI tools

- Founder mindset, comfortable deciding with incomplete information

- Fluent in German and English

- Based in or near Zürich

Your opportunity

This is your chance to design how a Treuhand works, with processes and tools you choose yourself. You join as co-founder with equity and start part-time. We agree on the details personally.

title: Flight Test Instrumentation & Data Engineer
description:
The Flight Test Instrumentation (FTI) & Data Engineer will be responsible for the end-to-end handling, quality assurance, accessibility, and long-term management of all flight data. The primary objective is to ensure that full-aircraft data, from the onboard sensors and DAQ systems to the final processing tools, is available to every engineering team through a reliable, efficient, and standardized workflow.

Tasks

Flight Test Instrumentation (FTI) & DAQ Pipeline 

- Manage the data pipeline from the physical sensor and Data Acquisition (DAQ) level for the full aircraft, ensuring seamless and accurate transmission into the telemetry and storage systems.

- Maintain sensor configuration, calibration records, and metadata to guarantee the accurate translation of raw physical signals into usable engineering units.

- Collaborate with hardware, software and integration teams to define sensor requirements, DAQ architectures, scaling, and telemetry bandwidth allocations.

- Troubleshoot and resolve data anomalies at the DAQ and sensor level (e.g., signal noise, dropouts, faulty scaling) before they propagate into downstream databases.

Data Infrastructure & Accessibility 

- Maintain reliable extraction of flight data from InfluxDB.

- Develop and maintain standardized local data structures for analysis, plotting, and visualization.

- Optimize access to large flight datasets while minimizing CPU and memory usage.

- Design and maintain an efficient local storage solution for processed flight data.

- Support future improvements to the flight data architecture as storage requirements, sensor counts, and analysis needs continue to evolve.

Data Quality & Analysis Support 

- Maintain derived datasets to ensure common calculations and signals are shared consistently across teams.

- Ensure strict timing synchronization and timestamp accuracy across all recorded data, from the sensor acquisition point to the database.

- Monitor data quality, completeness, and integrity throughout the entire pipeline.

- Provide fast data previews for rapid post-flight reviews.

- Enable efficient access to high-frequency sensor data for detailed engineering investigations.

- Support custom querying of processed datasets.

Requirements

Education & Experience 

- Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, Computer Science, Data Engineering, or a related technical field.

- 3+ years of professional experience in test instrumentation, data acquisition (DAQ), or sensor-to-database time-series data engineering (aerospace, automotive, or racing/motorsports preferred).

- Hands-on experience working directly with physical aircraft/vehicle sensor installations, DAQ hardware, and telemetry pipelines.

Technical & Domain Expertise 

1. Hardware, Sensors & DAQ Architecture

- Strong understanding of physical sensors (e.g., strain gauges, accelerometers, thermocouples, pressure transducers, RTDs, LVDTs, pitot-static tubes).

- Demonstrated knowledge of signal conditioning, sampling rate selection, anti-aliasing filtering, scaling, and sensor calibration procedures.

2. Data Infrastructure & Software Development

- Proficient in Python or MATLAB for data analysis, automated data processing, and visualization library development (e.g., Pandas, NumPy, SciPy).

- Experience working with time-series databases, specifically InfluxDB (or similar engines), including writing efficient queries (Flux/InfluxQL) and data retrieval pipelines.

- Solid foundation in data structures and memory/CPU optimization when handling high-memory high-frequency continuous time-series datasets.

3. Data Integrity & Signal Processing

- Experience with timestamping and clock synchronization protocols across distributed DAQ hardware and storage nodes.

- Knowledge of basic digital signal processing (DSP) concepts (filtering, FFT, spectral analysis, decimation/resampling).

Soft Skills & Work Style 

- Cross-functional communication: Ability to bridge the gap between hardware technicians, flight physics/aerodynamics engineers, and software teams.

- Detail-oriented mindset: Uncompromising rigor regarding calibration metadata, unit conversions, and data accuracy.

- Adaptability: Drive to continuously improve data infrastructure as aircraft sensor counts, test frequencies, and analytical needs expand.

Preferred / Bonus Qualifications 

- Knowledge of standard FAA / EASA flight test instrumentation requirements or military flight test standards (e.g. IRIG 106).

- Familiarity with dashboarding tools (e.g., Grafana) for rapid post-flight previews and real-time telemetry display.

- Experience with version control systems (Git) and CI/CD pipelines for internal engineering tool distribution.

- Direct experience with DAQ systems and digital bus protocols (CAN bus, ARINC 429, MIL-STD-1553, Ethernet/UDP, PCM).

- Familiarity with binary flight data formats (e.g., IRIG 106 Chapter 10/11, MDF/MF4, HDF5, Parquet, or custom binary loggers).

- Experience with performing on-aircraft hardware troubleshooting (e.g., tracking down ground loops, signal noise, dropouts, or faulty scaling).

title: Growth Marketer
description:
About us: 

Tebi is creating the first Connected Restaurant Management System that makes hospitality flow. In one seamless platform, Tebi embeds sales, reservations, kitchen prep, payments, and all the data that powers it, creating smooth service and intuitive insights.

Founded by Arnout Schuijff, co-founder of Adyen, and backed by €50 million in funding from Index Ventures & CapitalG, Tebi is built in service of hospitality first. Thousands of restaurants, cafés, bars, and coffee shops across the Netherlands, UK, Italy, Spain, Germany, Denmark and Finland already love running on Tebi.

About the role: 

Restaurant owners generally aren't on LinkedIn and they don't read e-books. They ask friends, search Google, and more and more often, they ask ChatGPT. We need someone who can find new ways to reach them and get those ideas live quickly.

We're hiring a Growth Marketer to build and ship our organic and non-paid growth experiments. This role is for a builder, not a strategist. You'd rather ship a working test today than a polished deck next week. You'll take ideas from the backlog to live, measure them honestly, and double down on what works. Using AI and no-code tools, you'll build pages, tools and campaigns yourself instead of relying on agencies and six-figure budgets.

You'll report to the Head of Marketing, who sets direction and priorities. You'll work in deep collaboration with our other growth marketers, product marketing and creative teammates, plus embed yourself in the wider org of Sales, Account Management, RevOps, Product, and more.

What you'll be doing: 

- Ship growth experiments, fast: Take ideas from our growth backlog and get them live: landing pages, tools, ads and content. Run plenty of them, keep what works and kill what doesn't.

- Get Tebi recommended by AI: Own our visibility in ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Gemini and Google's AI Overviews. Create and update content built to be cited, not just published, and track how often we show up compared with competitors.

- Build tools operators actually use: Build free tools, calculators and templates for restaurant owners, and scale our programmatic landing pages. Use no-code, AI and vibe coding tools to ship without waiting on engineering.

- Run creative campaigns: Help launch scrappy, unconventional campaigns across markets, from competitive campaigns to guerrilla and partner media, with the support of our Marketing team.

- Turn word of mouth into a channel: Test referral and sharing ideas that turn merchant word of mouth into a steady flow of demo requests. Work with our Product Growth team to build the winners into the product.

- Keep paid and organic working together: Support our performance agency with landing pages, creative tests and tracking.

- Measure everything: Keep the experiment log up to date: hypothesis, cost, result and next step. Set up tracking and UTMs properly so we know what actually drove each demo.

How we'll measure success: 

- Experiments shipped each month, and what we learned from them

- Demo requests from organic and other non-paid channels

- How often Tebi appears in AI answers for our category, by market

- Demos from free tools, the reservation widget and programmatic pages

What you’ll bring: 

- Think like a growth marketer but move like a hacker. You know what drives results and how to build just enough to prove it

- Ship rather than spec. A working prototype today beats a polished plan next week

- Have built and launched things yourself, like pages, tools, automations or campaigns, and can tell us what happened, including what didn't work

- Already use AI to work faster and have a point of view on how it's changing the way people find products

- Are hands-on with no-code and AI tools (Framer or Webflow, Zapier or Make, Claude or ChatGPT, Cursor or similar), without being precious about the stack

- Are comfortable with data and honest about results, in GA4, HubSpot, Looker or whatever gets the answer

- Have creative, sharp ideas and the discipline to ship the unglamorous parts too

- Take ownership and don't wait to be told what to do. No task is above or beneath you

- Speak fluent English. Another European language is a plus

Nice to have: 

- Experience with SEO, and with AEO or getting a brand cited by AI tools

- Experience marketing to small businesses, or a background in hospitality

- Vibe-coding projects you're proud of

We don't have a minimum number of years for this role. We care more about how you think and what you've built than how long you've been doing it. If this sounds like you but you don't tick every box, we'd still like to hear from you.

Benefits: 

- Start-up Equity

- Competitive Salary

- Lunch Provided in Office

- Team building events

- Unlimited time off

What is Restaurant Software? 

Restaurants and other merchants use various software systems such as Point of Sale (POS), Reservations, Kitchen Display Systems (KDS), Payments, Inventory, Staffing, and the list goes on. These systems all need to speak to each other which they frequently don’t. It’s a mess, and we are fixing it.

From buying a croissant at a cafe to having dinner with friends, it’s a €4 Trillion+ global market and a critical part of everyday life in today's economy.

How we use AI at Tebi 

We use AI the way our merchants use Tebi, to cut out the friction and get to what matters faster. We believe in a world where AI increases quality, efficiency and speed.

At Tebi, AI isn't a policy or a checkbox, it's just part of how we work. It helps us write, analyse, build, and improve but doesn’t make the last call. If there's a smarter way to do something, we want to find it.

Most People roles ask you to run processes someone else built. This one asks you to build them, and to own one of them outright: how Eye rewards and recognises its people. This role has two halves, and you’ll split your time roughly evenly between them.

The first half is Total Rewards. You’ll own compensation and benefits at Eye, including salary reviews, benchmarking, levelling, benefits and our equity program. What you’ll do 

- Own Total Rewards end to end: run the annual salary review, keep our benchmarks honest, and build levelling and salary bands that make sense to managers and employees alike.

title: Senior ML Engineer | Kimchi (Inference Stack Optimization)
description:
Why Kimchi?

Great models are raw ingredients. Kimchi is what happens when you ferment them with good engineering. We started inside CAST AI helping companies run LLMs on their own Kubernetes clusters; today we run our own coding harness on any model you pick, and we run the models underneath it ourselves.

Kimchi Inference 

One API line and a customer's existing client just works: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, MiniMax, Nemotron served serverless from our own GPU fleet (OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible, pay per token, spend visible per user, team, and key). When control matters, the same models run on the customer's own cluster instead. Behind that one line sits the machinery you'll own: SGLang and vLLM engines, B300 nodes, a shared cluster filesystem that holds every checkpoint exactly once, KV caches riding coding traffic with heavy prefix reuse, and the benchmark harness that gates every change we ship.

Made by Cast AI — a Miami-headquartered, globally distributed team across 34 countries that hit unicorn status in January 2026 with a $50B+ backed investment pushing its valuation past $1 billion. 

About the role

Throughput. Latency. Cold starts. Cost per token.

Move those four numbers in the right direction and two things happen: customers get faster, cheaper inference, and our margins improve. That's the entire thesis of this role. Every loader you tune, every scheduler decision you land, every kernel you stare at shows up in a customer's p99 and on our P&L. Your mandate is the inference stack's optimization, whatever it takes, and the technical direction of how we optimize it is yours to argue with data.

The problem: the checkpoints run 0.3-1.5 TB, and the "right" serving configuration depends on traffic shape, sequence-length distribution, batch dynamics, GPU SKU, memory bandwidth, and quantization tolerance, all variables that shift week to week. Most teams pick a configuration once, over-provision GPUs, and absorb the cost. We don't: we took Kimi-K3 (1.5 TB) from over an hour cold-to-serving to under twelve minutes with a shared filesystem, O_DIRECT weight loaders, and node-local JIT caches, and we're nowhere near done. Prefill/decode disaggregation and tiered KV caches are next.

Stack: Python; SGLang; vLLM; TensorRT-LLM; PyTorch; fastsafetensors; CUDA-adjacent tooling; Kubernetes; virtiofs shared filesystems; ClickHouse; OpenTelemetry; Prometheus; Grafana; GitLab CI.

Requirements

- You've built real ML systems for 5+ years, and your portfolio shows depth in inference or training infrastructure, not just model training notebooks.

- Your Python is production-grade: services, not scripts.

- You've run vLLM, SGLang, or TensorRT-LLM for real, and you have a working mental model of why an engine performs the way it does on a given GPU.

- You've measured quantization regressions, not just compression ratios.

- Multi-GPU and multi-node setups hold no fear: tensor and expert parallelism, collective communication, and their practical failure modes.

- You know where the bytes live (page caches, O_DIRECT, network filesystems under terabyte-scale reads) and how fast they move.

- You instrument before you optimize, and you can tell a real win from a benchmark artifact.

- A wide mandate excites you more than it unsettles you.

Nice to haves

- You've worked on LLM routing specifically: RouterBench-class evals, cost/quality/latency Pareto fronts.

- Calibration, abstention, or conformal methods in production decision systems.

- You've run online A/B loops with drift monitoring on a model that touches real money.

Responsibilities

- Push throughput. Continuous batching, chunked prefill, speculative decoding with draft models, CUDA-graph capture, and scheduler tuning across the engine
fleet. Find the ceiling on each GPU SKU, then raise it.

- Cut latency. Attack TTFT and inter-token latency separately; profile to find the actual bottleneck (compute, memory bandwidth, scheduling, storage, or
network) and fix it, not the one you assumed.

- Get more out of the KV cache. Hierarchical and paged attention, prefix caching on heavy-reuse coding traffic, eviction policies, quantized KV. A lot of the
unrealized throughput lives here, and you'll own it.

- Kill cold starts. Weight loaders (O_DIRECT, fastsafetensors-class), JIT and compile caches, shared-filesystem read paths. A 1.5 TB checkpoint has no business
taking an hour to reach serving.

- Quantize without regressing quality. INT8/INT4, FP8/FP4 across weights, activations, and KV, measured on real workloads, not just perplexity benchmarks.

- Scale across nodes. Distributed inference topologies, network-aware placement, prefill/decode disaggregation, checkpointing strategies that don't bottleneck
on storage or interconnect.

- Set the technical direction. Decide what we benchmark, what we adopt, and what we build ourselves. Bring the team along with strong writeups and reproducible
experiments.

What’s in it for you?

title: Senior Applied ML Engineer | Kimchi (Model Router)
description:
Why Kimchi?

Great models are raw ingredients. Kimchi is what happens when you ferment them with good engineering. We started inside CAST AI helping companies run LLMs on their own Kubernetes clusters; today we run our own coding harness on any model you pick, and the router deciding which model answers each request is ours too.

The Auto Router 

Our promise is one enforcement layer for your AI: budgets, spend attribution, and model routing, applied before a request ever hits a model. The Auto Router makes the call: for every request, which model serves it. Eight open-source models whose input prices span more than 20×, cached input up to 50× cheaper than fresh, frontier providers on customers' own keys, and a coding agent that fires hundreds of requests before its task is done. Frontier-level task success at a fraction of the token cost: that sentence is the product, and it stays true only if the model inside the router keeps getting better. That model is yours.

Made by Cast AI — a Miami-headquartered, globally distributed team across 34 countries that hit unicorn status in January 2026 with a $50B+ backed investment pushing its valuation past $1 billion. 

About the role

Every request gets a decision: which model serves it.

This is an applied-ML seat, not an infrastructure one. Platform engineers own the proxy, the streaming path, and the fleet. You own the model inside them: the training data, the objective, the evaluation, and the iteration loop that ships a better router every cycle.

The problem: routing is a prediction problem wearing a product's clothes. For every request you predict the quality each candidate model would deliver, what it would cost, and how fast it would decode, and you have to be right enough, in aggregate, that the savings are real and the quality never dips below frontier. The data is messy: rollout outcomes from benchmark harnesses, per-request records from the live fleet, override signals, and token streams whose speed depends on the serving concurrency at the moment. Speed itself is a correctness variable: on deadline-bound agentic work, a model that decodes three times slower doesn't do the same work slower, it does less work. That's why naive cost-per-token objectives quietly optimize for the wrong thing. And the bar for evidence is high: a router change ships only after production-parity evaluation with error bars, then gets held to its numbers in live traffic.

Stack: Python; PyTorch; SQL at scale (ClickHouse); OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible LLM APIs; benchmark and rollout harnesses (RouterBench-class); GitLab CI.

Requirements

- You've spent 5+ years in applied ML or ML research, and you've trained, evaluated, and shipped models that make real-time decisions (ranking, recommendation, bandits, pricing, or LLM routing) and you can tell that story with receipts.

- Strong Python and SQL at scale: you can pull, clean, and interrogate millions of request-level records without waiting on anyone.

- You know the difference between a model that got better and an eval that got easier.

Nothing ships on vibes.

task) so poisoned labels never reach the policy.

economics in the picture.

ship.

which model it picks today.

the data path must support.

What’s in it for you?

The Vinted Group is made up of three business units that support this mission:

Vinted Marketplace is Europe’s leading platform for second-hand fashion and a go-to destination for all kinds of pre-loved items, with a growing range of categories. Our platform connects millions of members across 20+ markets, helping great items find a new life.

Vinted Go enhances the shipping experience with a vast network of over 500,000 pick-up and drop-off points, partnering with more than 60 carriers across Europe, with added services like item verification for peace of mind on high-value pieces.

Vinted Pay is the newest part of the Vinted Group, dedicated to bringing secure, reliable payments to buyers and sellers across Europe. Seamlessly integrated into the Vinted app, it helps keep every transaction safe, efficient, and easy for our members.

Founded in 2008 in Lithuania, Vinted began as a way for friends to find new homes for clothes they no longer needed. In 2019, we became Lithuania's first unicorn! Today, our headquarters remain in Vilnius, and we've grown with offices across Europe, supported by a team of over 2,000 people. 

Information about the position 

Our team’s mission is to align Vinted’s values, business goals, and Employer Value Proposition with our people’s real work experience. We translate Vinted’s truth into an inspiring story that attracts the right people, helps them grow, and instils them with pride.

You’ll take an active role in Employer Branding at Vinted, with a particular focus on attracting engineering and data science talent. You’ll be based in Amsterdam, where our data science team is growing, but your work will reach candidates around the world.

Vinted has become an ecosystem with vertically integrated shipping and payments. This requires us to adapt our EVP to three very distinct brands and even more diversified hiring needs. Your job is to turn that into creative campaigns and stories that make specific audiences want to work here.

Our next big focus is storytelling. Bringing the skills and challenges our teams face to life! What is a day in the life of a cybersecurity analyst? How does an anti-money laundering expert keep members’ wallets safe? What does it take to build the data science behind a marketplace used by millions? And what stories does each of our locations need?

Partnering with Talent Acquisition, engineering and data science leaders, People, Marketing, PR, Internal Comms, and Brand & Design, you’ll make sure those stories are told and that our presence is strong where we hire.

In this position, you’ll 

- Be the guardian of Vinted’s employer brand, ensuring consistency and visibility across all platforms, like LinkedIn and Instagram

- Strong brand-building skills, with a clear vision of global vs local branding differentiation

- Use your sound understanding of branding and our editorial guidelines to write clear and engaging copy for things such as blogs, advertising campaigns, employer branding assets, email campaigns, event materials, online company profiles, as well as our careers pages.

- Create bespoke or support partnership events such as meetups, webinars, and networking events

- Plan and run recruitment advertising, such as targeted LinkedIn campaigns and sponsorships with third-party publications and organisations, aimed at technical audiences.

- Define where our global employer brand ends and local adaptation begins, so each location can tell its story while staying consistent with Vinted’s.

- Shape our content calendar around hiring needs and our location strategy.

- Track what works, using results to sharpen the next activation, and share learnings with the wider Employer Branding team.

About you 

- Passionate about all things Employer Branding!

- You love storytelling: finding stories and having a keen eye for telling them in ways that stand out. You can show campaigns or activations you conceived and delivered.

- Background in building and nurturing online and offline communities, and delivering innovative events and social media campaigns.

- A clear view of global vs local branding, and experience working across markets.

- Adept at identifying new talent attraction channels, especially for engineering and data science audiences.

- Comfortable using data to set goals and judge what worked.

- Ability to juggle multiple projects with strong stakeholder management, and to work confidently with engineering and data science leaders.

- Excited by change, a fast pace, and learning new ways of doing things.

- Excellent knowledge of social media and digital channels, including LinkedIn, Glassdoor, Indeed, and Meta.

- Excellent written and verbal English communication skills (English is Vinted’s official working language).

Work perks

- 25 days of paid annual leave

- Newest MacBook models

- Home office support: we provide IT workstation equipment and a personal budget of up to €540 for home workplace furniture

Better balance holidays with workdays by working remotely! Up to 90 days per year in the EU, of these, 21 days can be spent globally. For non-EU citizens, it's 21 days worldwide. This can be combined with time off for vacation or personal time.

Individual learning budget 

Each year, you’ll be given a learning budget (starting at €3,000), and a total of up to 10 working days over a 2-year period to support your personal and professional development.

- AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

We're looking for a senior B2B Growth Marketer to build and scale demand generation for ElevenLabs in the Benelux Region. This is a hands-on, in-region role focused on generating enterprise pipeline, growing our brand with technical buyers, and creating programs that become benchmarks for B2B marketing in AI.

Requirements

title: Sr. Software Engineer II / Tech lead, Agentic Platform (Poland, Remote, B2B)
description:
Who we are 

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role: 

We're building the next chapter: an agentic platform that understands operational context and takes action, with the ambition to make physical operations increasingly autonomous. External Platform EMEA owns critical capabilities behind that transition. Depending on the team, your work could include:

- Reporting and intelligence. Own the reporting engine and products that turn the complexity of a fleet into answers customers can act on.

- Enterprise administration. Build how customers configure and control Samsara at scale, from permissions and device metadata to AI-assisted onboarding.

- Developer and agent platform. Build APIs, event systems, integrations, and tools that give applications and AI agents access to operational data and actions.

- Business-critical infrastructure. Own billing, license assignment, and usage metering: systems central to how Samsara sells, delivers, and grows its products.

The long-term opportunity is rooted in the physical world. Deployed hardware, data generated at the edge, and years of operational expertise form a foundation that's hard to replicate. As AI advances, it expands what we can build on that foundation. This is a place to develop deep engineering expertise while helping shape a platform with years of ambitious work ahead.

AI is also central to how we build. We expect engineers to push tools like Codex, Claude Code, and Cursor throughout design, implementation, testing, and production investigations, taking on more ambitious work while owning the quality of what they ship.

In this role, you will: 

- Lead technical discussions with teammates to identify gaps in our telematics data platform and influence roadmap by setting direction and recommending solutions

- Collaborate with other engineering teams to make design decisions and understand downstream implications in our product to ensure a seamless customer experience

- Ship features that deliver value to customers, consistently refining them based on gathered feedback.

- Deliver full stack features across multiple tiers (front-end, back-end and mobile). GoLang, GraphQL, Typescript, React and ReactNative among other technologies. Direct experience with these technologies is not required.

- Be responsible for maintaining the production systems that your team owns and provide operational support.

- Make an impact on our core architecture, roadmap, and the wider engineering community.

- Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices 

- Hire, develop and lead an inclusive, engaged, and high performing team 

Minimum requirements for the role: 

- 8+ years of relevant engineering experience , including hands-on work building and operating complex enterprise systems .

- A track record of turning partially defined customer or business challenges into technical direction, execution plans, and measurable outcomes with substantial autonomy.

- Strong system design judgment, including service boundaries, dependencies, failure modes, performance, and safe changes to production systems.

- Experience leading delivery through deep ownership of a critical system or coordination across multiple services and teams, balancing immediate needs with long-term architecture.

- Ability to improve other engineers’ effectiveness through mentoring, design reviews, and clear technical decisions.

- Extensive use of AI throughout engineering, including complex investigations and design exploration, with the ability to validate results and help teammates adopt effective workflows.

An ideal candidate also has: 

- Experience building customer-facing web and mobile workflow applications

- Contributed heavily to driving significant value to their customers

- Curiosity about our customers, and is eager to improve their day-to-day experience

- Seeks to iterate on new products based on customer feedback

- Exceptional problem-solving abilities and meticulous attention to detail.Strong communication skills for effective teamwork and project collaboration.

- Enthusiastic and committed to innovating in a fast-paced and dynamic team environment.

- Experience in any one of these areas is a plus. Exposure should come from enterprise-scale, production work.

- Reporting and data systems: Reporting products, analytics, query execution, data retrieval, or turning complex datasets into useful customer experiences.

- Enterprise administration: Permissions and access control, entity metadata, configuration frameworks, or customer onboarding and setup automation.

- Developer and agent platforms: Public APIs, event-driven systems, integrations, Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, or tools that let AI agents access data and take action.

- Billing and monetization: Billing systems, license assignment, product entitlements, or usage metering supporting how a business sells and delivers its products.

- Full-stack product development: Building complete customer experiences across frontend interfaces, backend services, and data models. 

The range of annual base salary for full-time employees for this position is below. Please note that base pay offered may vary depending on factors including your city of residence, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. This role is also eligible for an initial RSU grant with no vesting cliff, and ongoing refresh opportunities tied to performance, subject to plan terms and conditions. Learn more about our total rewards and benefits below.

Annual Base Salary

638 350 zł—751 000 zł PLN

Total Rewards 

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working 

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

Belonging at Samsara

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. Accommodations 

Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email accessibleinterviewing@samsara.com or click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.

Our Commitment to Authenticity 

We use Tofu , a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara’s Candidate Privacy Notice for more information.

title: Software Engineer, Analytics
description:
Software Engineer, Analytics 

In Brief 

- 
We’re an early-stage startup on a mission to make healthcare proactive by empowering physicians, nurses, and care team members with real-time data to save lives.

- 
You will lead the development of our clinical AI/ML product analytics infrastructure, frameworks, and tools to enable our client success, product, clinical, and technology teams to uplevel our decision making through better insights.

Who We Are 

Bayesian Health ’s mission is to improve patient outcomes by empowering clinicians with the insights they need to make the right decision for the right patient at the point-of-care. We’re a diverse team of clinicians, engineers, machine learning experts, product designers, and performance improvement leaders committed to enabling smarter, patient-specific care delivery through unlocking the power of data.

We’re funded by top tier tech and biotech investors: Obvious Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz, American Medical Association’s venture arm, Catalio Partners, and LifeForce Capital. Our company has won many awards; most recent recognitions include: Forbes AI Top 50, World Economic Forum Tech Pioneer, Time Best Inventions, BioTech AI Company of the Year.

Read more about our recent publication in Nature Medicine that associates our products with lives saved. 

What you'll do 

As a Senior Software Engineer, Analytics, you will work closely with client success, product managers, clinicians, data scientists, and other software engineers to build infrastructure, frameworks, and tools to improve client analytics, facilitate clinical case reviews, and support product investigation. This role is crucial to provide internal visibility into product performance that will drive expansion of our clinical AI/ML module offerings and revenue growth.

Responsibilities 

- 
Product performance monitoring and optimization: Partner with client success and clinical product subject matter experts to implement the infrastructure, queries, and automation to monitor the KPIs and success metrics of our products across multiple clinical domains and clients.

- 
Clinical case review and investigation : Build frameworks and tools to empower our clinical team to independently review and investigate clinical cases reported by our clients and identify cases with certain criteria that need further evaluation.

- 
Data platform and analytics technical foundations: Propose and implement foundational improvements and innovations to boost our data platform scalability with expanding products and clients and uplevel our team analytics capabilities.

- 
Drive product analytics development cross-functionally: Work closely with Client Success, Clinical, Product, Data Science, and Engineering to drive alignment on product analytics at the company level.

Minimum qualifications 

- 
BS in Computer Science or other relevant technical discipline.

- 
5+ years of experience in building scalable, secure analytics infrastructure and tools on a cloud platform (preferably AWS) to produce monitoring metrics and investigational data from complex data models and queries for live products and customers.

- 
Proficient in Python and SQL.

- 
Deep knowledge in modern data and analytics technologies, such as cloud-based data warehouses, transformation frameworks (e.g. dbt), workflow orchestration tools, and BI tools like Tableau or Quicksight, and keen ability to integrate with existing infrastructure to enhance capabilities.

- 
Experience working with sensitive data that contains PHI/PII.

- 
Excellent communication skills and a proven ability to collaborate with cross-functional teams (data science, product, clinical) to translate requirements into robust technical solutions

Preferred qualifications 

- 
Experience in leveraging LLMs in distributed data processing and analytics systems.

- 
Experience building analytics technology for clinical/health data.

- 
Experience handling ambiguity and uncertainty in a startup.
